About this tool

London today, in one place.

London Dashboard brings together the information that can change a day in the city: the weather ahead, problems on the transport network, travel to the airports, current air-quality conditions and events happening across London.

It is designed as a quick starting point rather than another full journey planner. Use it to understand what is happening, spot anything that may affect your plans and decide where to look next.

Useful for
  • Checking conditions before leaving
  • Monitoring transport disruption
  • Planning airport journeys
  • Browsing events by date
How to use it

From a quick check to a firmer plan.

  1. 01

    Start with Now

    Check the latest London weather forecast, current Tube conditions and the air-quality reading before deciding what to do or how to travel.

  2. 02

    Review Travel and Flights

    Look for disruption affecting rail and London transport, then check the airport information relevant to your journey.

  3. 03

    Search for events

    Choose a single date or a range of up to 31 days, filter Ticketmaster results by category and browse the available pages.

  4. 04

    Continue with the right tool

    Move to Escape the Crowds, the Fare Calculator, Smart Navigation or London by Mood when you need more detailed help.

What it uses

Established London data sources.

The dashboard brings together information from sources including the Met Office, Transport for London, National Rail, the London Air Quality Network and the Ticketmaster Discovery API.

Some information is cached briefly to keep the dashboard fast and reduce unnecessary requests to external services.

What to know

Useful context, not a guarantee.

Live services can be delayed, incomplete or temporarily unavailable. Check the relevant operator before beginning a time-critical journey.

The air-quality figure is the highest current index reported across participating London monitoring sites, not a street-level reading. Ticketmaster is useful for bookable events but is not a complete list of everything happening in London.

Worked example

Checking a Saturday plan before leaving.

You plan to cross London for an afternoon museum visit and have an evening booking, but the forecast looks unsettled.

  1. Open Now to compare the next few hours of weather with the current air-quality reading.
  2. Check Travel for disruption on the lines and rail services that could affect both journeys.
  3. If an airport transfer is part of the day, review Flights and then confirm the final timing with the airport or carrier.
  4. Use Events only if you need another bookable option; use the independent Events edit for a smaller selection beyond the obvious.

The useful result: one quick risk check identifies what needs changing and which details still require an official source.

Common questions

What the dashboard can—and cannot—tell you.

How live is the London Dashboard?

The dashboard requests current information from its external sources, with short caching where needed for speed and reliability. Update timing varies by provider, so time-critical details should be confirmed with the relevant operator.

Can the dashboard replace a journey planner?

No. It gives a rapid overview of weather, disruption, airports, air quality and events. Use TfL, National Rail or the relevant operator for a detailed route and final departure information.

Does the Events tab show everything happening in London?

No. It shows bookable events supplied through Ticketmaster and is useful for date and category searches, but it is not a complete cultural calendar. The separate London Advanced Events page provides a smaller independently selected edit.
